planMarkdown:
# LEGION-15 plan — convert every tick-bounded wait in `processes.test.ts` to an await on its event

Baseline: `main` at `52c5e03e` (pull request #981 merged). File: `packages/daemon/src/daemon/__tests__/processes.test.ts` (13,091 lines). Line numbers below are at that commit; re-grep before editing (`grep -n 'flushEventLoop' processes.test.ts`).

## Decisions needed

None that block implementation. One finding (below) offers the architect an optional relaxation of acceptance 5 for a single site; the plan works without it.

## Constraint (acceptance 5)

No production code changes. Every hook lives in the test file's shared `manager()` fixture or in a test's own injected fake. The pull request's file list is exactly one file: `packages/daemon/src/daemon/__tests__/processes.test.ts`. Where a chain is unobservable without a production seam, this plan names it under **Findings** and gives a test-only fallback; the implementer does not add the seam.

## Population

53 tick-bounded sites: 20 `flushEventLoopUntil(...)` and 33 `flushEventLoop(n)` (default 2 000 ticks unless a count is given). Disposition: **33 convert** to an await (every `until` site, 8 fixed drains that follow a released gate, and 5 idle-retire trailing drains folded into the preceding await), **19 stay** as negative in-memory drains with a one-line comment, **1 deleted** (nothing is in flight). `flushEventLoopUntil` has no caller afterwards and is deleted; `flushEventLoop` stays for the 19 negative drains with its doc comment rewritten to say so.

## Fixture design — one convention, extending #981's resolver

#981 added `windowCounter()` (`count`, `increment()`, `reached(n)`) and `ProcessManager.drainSpawns()`. The single primitive stays a counter with an awaitable threshold; it is generalised and wired into every injected dep the fixture already wraps. Names are fixed; the implementer must not introduce a second shape (no ad-hoc `Promise.withResolvers` gates for counting — those stay only where a fake must *block*, e.g. `probeGate`, `saveGate`).

```ts
/** Counts occurrences of one event and lets a test await the Nth as a real event. `reached(n)`
 * resolves on the macrotask AFTER the count reaches n (one `onceEventLoop()`), so the awaiting
 * test resumes after every microtask continuation that event unblocked in the code under test
 * (the synchronous re-check that follows a probe, the locator write that follows a spawn) — but
 * not after any further real I/O; await that I/O's own event instead. A wait that never resolves
 * fails on bun's per-test timeout with the assertion unreached, never a false green. */
interface EventCounter {
  readonly count: number;
  increment(): void;
  reached(n: number): Promise<void>;
  /** `reached(count + 1)` captured now — for "the next one after this trigger" when the prior
   * count is incidental to the test's story. Call it BEFORE the trigger. */
  next(): Promise<void>;
}
function eventCounter(): EventCounter;              // was windowCounter(); renamed at its 9 call sites

/** One injected dep observed at both ends. `issued` counts calls as they are made (before the
 * test's fake runs — the event to await when the fake blocks on a gate the test releases later);
 * `completed` counts them as they resolve (the event to await when the assertions need the call's
 * result to have reached the code under test). */
interface CallObserver { readonly issued: EventCounter; readonly completed: EventCounter }
```

`manager()` returns, in addition to today's fields (and `idleWorkerFixture`/`workerCapFixture` pass them through):

| field | wraps | key | increments |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `saves: CallObserver` | `deps.saveState` (the test's override or the default no-op) | — | `issued` before calling the injected fn, `completed` after it resolves |
| `runs(verb): CallObserver` | `deps.run` (extends the wrapper already at line 460) | `command[0] === "tmux" ? command[3] : command[0]` — `"list-panes"`, `"kill-pane"`, `"new-window"`, `"split-window"`, `"has-session"`, `"jj"` | `issued` first thing, `completed` last thing (after the jj mkdir side effects and stdout defaulting) |
| `sleeps(ms): EventCounter` | `deps.sleep`, only when the test injected one (no injection = real timers = nothing counted; a `reached` then fails loud on the test timeout) | duration in ms | on call (= the wait was armed) |
| `published(type): EventCounter` | `deps.natsPublish` (the test's override or the default `publications.push`) | `JSON.parse(json).type`, `"?"` when absent | after the injected fn |

Plus `registrationDeadlineMs(config: DaemonConfig): number` = `config.workerBootTimeoutSeconds * 1000 * config.workerBootRegistrationDeadlineIntervals` (360 000 for `config(stateDir)`), so a test names the deadline sleep instead of a literal.

Keyed observers are lazy: `runs(verb)` / `sleeps(ms)` / `published(type)` create the counter on first use so a test can request `reached` before any event. Wrapping happens once in `manager()` after the `...overrides` spread — a test's own `run`/`saveState`/`sleep`/`natsPublish` fake keeps working unchanged and is observed from outside; a fake that branches on its own call count (`listPanesCalls === 2`, `saveStateCalls === 2`, `sleepCalls === 1`) keeps that local counter for branching and the test awaits through the observer.

Idioms: `await runs("kill-pane").completed.reached(1)`; `await saves.issued.reached(2)`; `await sleeps(registrationDeadlineMs(cfg)).reached(2)`; `const retired = worker.saves.completed.next(); worker.clock.fire(600_000); await retired;`. Use `reached(n)` when n is part of the test's story (the 2nd new-window, the 3rd probe); use `next()` when the prior count is incidental.

Also kept: `processes.drainSpawns()` after a `new-window` await for root spawns/resurrections (#981's pairing). Not extended: `manualSleep()` (it controls a clock; `sleeps` observes one), `fakeWorkerRpcClient`, `FakeRuntime` (its `spawn` is wrapped in-test where needed, following the `client.shutdown` wrap precedent at line 213).

## Site dispositions

Legend: **(a)** convert — await the named event; **(b)** keep — pure in-memory drain, add the one-line comment; **(c)** keep — negative wait whose chain does no file write, add the comment; **(x)** delete. "Chain" is what runs un-awaited during the wait. Fixture default `saveState` is a no-op; a real state-file write happens only where a test injects a writing `saveState` (none of these do — the writes they race are `spawnRoot`/`launchWorker` fs provisioning and secret files, `pruneWrittenSecretFiles`'s `rm`, and injected `run`/`sleep` fakes).

| 1508 | retires an older generation's launch as stale when a park-then-re-admit starts a newer one first | `until(existsSync && content === "boot-gen-2")`, default 5 000 ticks | generation 2's `writeSecretFile` — a real `mkdir`+`writeFile` in `TmuxRuntime.preparePane` (runtime-tmux.ts:284), imported from `secrets.ts` directly; no injected dep runs between that write and the lane-serialised `split-window` (which is blocked behind gen 1 by design) | **(a′)** — see Finding 1 | `await waitFor(() => existsSync(architectFile) && readFileSync(architectFile, "utf8") === "boot-gen-2")` where `waitFor` is a new helper: check, `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 5))`, repeat, no tick cap — bounded by bun's per-test timeout (the spec's Errors row). Reserved for effects with no DI seam; this is its only caller. The assertion at 1513 stays. |
| 7126 | retires an unconfirmed worker boot at the first watchdog interval once its handle belongs to another process and its socket refuses, relaunching the same role | `until(claim.launchFailures === 1 && locator && !sameProcess)`, 50 000 | watchdog probe (FakeRuntime, in-memory) → `retireUnconfirmedBoot` → `persist` → `promoteWorkerQueue` → `launchWorker`: real `provisionWorkspace` fs → `runtime.spawn` (FakeRuntime) → locator write | (a) | wrap the test's `runtime.spawn` (precedent: `client.shutdown` wrap) to `spawns.increment()` after the original resolves; `await spawns.reached(2)`; the locator write is the synchronous continuation `reached`'s deferral covers |

## Findings (production hooks the constraint forbids)

1. **Site 1508 — `writeSecretFile` has no injectable seam.** `TmuxRuntime.preparePane` (runtime-tmux.ts:284) calls `writeSecretFile` from `secrets.ts` directly; `TmuxRuntimeDeps` carries `readProcessStat`/`readProcessCmdline`/`connectWorkerRpc` but no `writeSecret`. The test's own gates cannot observe the write (the next injected call, `split-window`, is lane-serialised behind generation 1 by design). Test-only fallback used by this plan: `waitFor`, a real-timer poll bounded by bun's per-test timeout — synchronises on the file's content, not on a tick count, and never passes silently. A three-line `writeSecret?: typeof writeSecretFile` dep on `TmuxRuntimeDeps` (defaulting to the import) would make it `secrets.written.reached(1)` under the same convention; that is a production file change and is not made here. Architect's call whether to authorise it in a follow-up; nothing blocks on it.
2. **Fire-and-forget chains have no production promise** — `armRootRegistrationDeadline`/`armControllerRegistrationDeadline`/`armIdleRetire` fire `void timedOut.then(...)`, `WorkerBootWatchdog.arm` runs `void watch()`. This is why every positive wait awaits a *dep-level effect* (a run verb, a save, a sleep, a publish) rather than "the chain finished", and why the 19 negative drains remain drains: their decline is a synchronous check with no effect to observe. Not a defect; recorded so nobody proposes a `drainDeadlines()` hook to "finish" this issue.
